l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Nephi is left alone after the people divide and goes toward his house pondering the things the Lord has shown him. God blesses him for declaring the word with unwearyingness, and Nephi declares the Lord’s warning of destruction to the people. When they try to cast him into prison, the Spirit conveys him away, and he continues declaring the word among all the people.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: God tells Nephi that he has seen Nephi’s faithful service and will bless him forever. God grants Nephi power over the people and declares that whatever Nephi seals or loosens on earth will be sealed or loosened in heaven.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The people of the Nephites are described as wicked, engaging in secret works of darkness, murderings, plunderings, and other iniquities. They harden their hearts, refuse to hearken to Nephi, revile him, and seek to imprison him.

l: people (scattered multitudes), The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The scattered multitudes are visited by Nephi after he returns from the direction of his house. Nephi declares to them the word of the Lord concerning their destruction if they do not repent, but they do not hearken.

l: division among the people, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: A division arises among the people, causing them to divide hither and thither and leave Nephi alone.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The word of the Lord comes to Nephi through a voice and commands him to declare that the people must repent or be smitten unto destruction. Nephi declares this word to the people, but they refuse to hearken.

l: Nephi's power, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: God gives Nephi power over the people, including power to declare that the earth, a temple, a mountain, or the people will be smitten according to the Lord’s will. Nephi also has power through the Spirit to escape when the people seek to imprison him.

l: famine, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: God tells Nephi that he may smite the earth with famine according to the wickedness of the people.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The Lord declares through Nephi that the people will be smitten unto destruction unless they repent. Nephi repeatedly declares this warning to the people.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The Lord commands the people to repent or be smitten unto destruction. The people do not repent and instead harden their hearts against the words declared by Nephi.

l: death of the chief judge, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The people had previously been told by Nephi about the death of the chief judge, but even that great miracle did not cause them to hearken to the words of the Lord.

l: Seezoram, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The chief judge’s death is identified as the great miracle Nephi had performed in telling the people about it.

l: contentions, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: After the people refuse to hearken to Nephi’s words, contentions begin among them, and they become divided against themselves.

l: slaying with the sword, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: As contentions increase, the people become divided against themselves and begin to slay one another with the sword.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The people of Nephi suffer wars, famine, and destruction caused by the secret band of robbers and their own wickedness. Nephi prays for famine and later prays for rain after the people repent, humble themselves, and eliminate the band of Gadianton. The Lord ends the famine, and the people prosper, rejoice, and enjoy peace as the church spreads. Later, dissenters and Lamanite descendants form a powerful band of robbers, bringing destruction and fear, while the people again grow forgetful, proud, and wicked.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Nephi prays that famine will replace destruction by the sword, and later prays for the famine to cease after the people repent. The people esteem him as a great prophet and man of God with power and authority from God.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The Lord causes a famine after Nephi prays, then turns away his anger and sends rain when the people repent. He causes the land to bring forth fruit and grain.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The people of Nephi suffer famine and destruction, remember the Lord and Nephi, and plead for relief. After repenting and humbling themselves, they prosper, spread across the land, and enjoy peace, but later become involved in renewed wickedness and are threatened by robbers.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The Lamanites suffer the famine and destruction along with the Nephites. Some Lamanite descendants join with dissenters and become part of a great band of robbers.

l: secret band of robbers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The secret band of robbers carries on destruction and wickedness, causing wars throughout the land. The people sweep away the band of Gadianton, making it extinct and concealing its secret plans in the earth.

l: church of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The church spreads throughout the land, and most Nephites and Lamanites belong to it during a period of exceedingly great peace.

l: the land, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The land suffers war, famine, dryness, and destruction, but later receives rain and again brings forth fruit and grain. The people rebuild its waste places and spread across it from the sea west to the sea east.

l: wars, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Wars occur throughout the land among the people of Nephi and continue for multiple years because of the secret band of robbers. Later, dissenters and Lamanite descendants commence another war against their brethren.

l: famine, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: A great famine comes upon the land after Nephi prays for it, causing many people to perish and leading them to remember the Lord. The famine ceases when the people repent and the Lord sends rain.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Destruction is first carried out by the secret band of robbers and by the sword, then becomes severe through famine. Later, the robbers cause great destruction among the Nephites and Lamanites, killing many and taking others captive.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The people repent and humble themselves in sackcloth when famine and destruction threaten them. Their repentance leads Nephi to pray for relief, and the Lord turns away his anger.

l: peace, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Peace follows the Lord's removal of the famine, and the people rejoice, prosper, and rebuild. The church spreads during several years of peace, though some doctrinal contentions and later strife arise.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The people's iniquity brings evil, destruction, and fear upon them. After briefly remembering the Lord, they again forget him, grow stronger in iniquity and pride, and ripen for destruction.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The unit concerns the children of men and their tendency to forget the Lord their God during prosperity, becoming proud, wicked, and slow to do good. The Lord their God blesses and prospers the people, chastens them with afflictions, and commands the earth, waters, mountains, treasures, and people according to his word. Repentance and hearkening to the Lord are declared so that men might be saved, while those who do evil face endless misery and everlasting damnation. In the great and last day, some will be cast off from the presence of the Lord, while those who have done good shall have everlasting life.

l: the children of men, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The children of men are unsteady, quick to do iniquity, slow to do good, quick to heed the evil one, and prone to pride and forgetfulness of the Lord their God. They do not desire the Lord their God to rule and guide them, and they are described as less than the dust of the earth.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The Lord their God blesses and prospers those who trust in him, protects them from enemies, and does all things for the welfare and happiness of his people. He chastens people with afflictions so they will remember him, and by his word and voice he commands the earth, waters, mountains, treasures, and people.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The people are blessed and prospered by the Lord in their fields, flocks, herds, wealth, safety, and peace. During ease and great prosperity, they harden their hearts, forget the Lord, and trample under their feet the Holy One.

l: the evil one, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The evil one is one whose words the children of men are quick to heed, leading them to set their hearts upon the vain things of the world.

l: the dust of the earth, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The dust of the earth moves hither and thither at the command of the great and everlasting God. It is used as a comparison showing that the children of men are less than it.

l: earth, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The earth moves, shakes, and has its foundations rocked at the voice of the Lord. At his command it can go back to lengthen the day, and it obeys when told to move.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Iniquity causes people to harden their hearts, forget the Lord, reject his counsels, and do evil. Because of iniquity, a treasure may be cursed, and a person may be cursed or cut off from the Lord's presence.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Repentance is declared so that men might be saved from being unable to be saved because of iniquity. Those who repent and hearken to the voice of the Lord their God are blessed and shall be saved.

l: good works, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Good works are sought for men to be brought unto repentance and restored unto grace for grace according to their works.

l: the great and last day, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: In the great and last day, some will be cast out and cast off from the presence of the Lord.

l: endless misery, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Endless misery is the state to which some who are cast off from the presence of the Lord will be consigned.

l: eternal life, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Everlasting life is promised to those who have done good.

l: everlasting damnation, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Everlasting damnation is the consequence stated for those who have done evil.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Samuel, a Lamanite, returns to Zarahemla at the Lord’s command and warns the Nephites to repent and have faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. He prophesies that the sword of justice, destruction, famine, pestilence, and the curse of the land will come upon the Nephites because of their wickedness, pride, iniquity, and rejection of the prophets. The Lord declares that the righteous preserve Zarahemla and that repentance can spare those who turn to him. Samuel also teaches that riches and hidden treasures will become slippery and be lost when the people set their hearts upon them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The Nephites remain in great wickedness while the Lamanites observe the commandments of God. They reject Samuel, cast out and persecute prophets, set their hearts upon riches, and face destruction unless they repent.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The Lord commands Samuel to return and prophesy to the Nephites. He warns of judgment, promises to spare those who repent, and declares that the righteous preserve Zarahemla.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Jesus Christ will come into the world, suffer many things, and be slain for his people. Samuel teaches that salvation from destruction requires repentance and faith on the Lord Jesus Christ.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Zarahemla is warned because many of its people harden their hearts against the Lord. It is spared because of the righteous within it, but it will be ripe for destruction if the righteous are cast out.

l: the land, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The land is cursed because of the people’s wickedness and abominations. Things hidden or possessed by the wicked become slippery and cannot be retained.

l: the sword of justice, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The sword of justice hangs over the Nephites. The Lord declares that it will fall upon them within four hundred years unless they repent.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Destruction is promised to the Nephites and their cities because of wickedness, abominations, and rejection of the Lord. The fourth generation of their enemies will behold and visit their destruction.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Repentance and returning to the Lord can turn away his anger and spare the people. Those who do not repent lose the opportunity for salvation.

l: faith on the Lord Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Faith on the Lord Jesus Christ is identified with repentance as the means by which the people can be saved from the destruction that awaits them.

l: the coming of Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The coming of Jesus Christ is declared as glad tidings. He will come into the world, suffer many things, and be slain for his people.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The word of the Lord is declared by Samuel to testify of the people’s sins and iniquities. The people reject those who declare it when it condemns their deeds.

l: the righteous, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The righteous preserve Zarahemla from destruction. The Lord will spare those who repent, but the city will be destroyed if the righteous are cast out.

l: the curse of the land, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The curse of the land comes because of the people’s wickedness and abominations. It causes treasures, riches, tools, and swords to become slippery and unavailable to the wicked.

l: treasures, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Treasures hidden in the earth will not be found again by the wicked because of the curse of the land. Those who set their hearts upon riches hide treasures while fleeing enemies and lose them.

l: riches, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The Nephites remember their riches rather than the Lord and set their hearts upon them. The Lord curses their riches so that they become slippery and cannot be retained.

l: the holy prophets, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The Nephites cast out, mock, stone, and slay the prophets. Later they regret not repenting when the prophets warned them.

l: iniquity, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Iniquity causes the Lord to curse the land and the people’s riches. The people seek happiness in doing iniquity, contrary to the nature of righteousness.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Wickedness and abominations bring a curse upon the land and warnings of destruction upon Zarahemla, Gideon, and the surrounding cities.

l: salvation, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The people procrastinate the day of their salvation until it is everlastingly too late. Samuel teaches that repentance and faith on the Lord Jesus Christ are necessary for salvation.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Samuel, the Lamanite, prophesies of the coming, birth, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ and gives signs that will accompany these events. He calls the people to repent and teaches that believers may receive everlasting life through the name and merits of Jesus Christ. He describes darkness, a new star, thunderings and lightnings, earthquakes, tempests, broken rocks, changed landscapes, opened graves, and other signs. He teaches that people are free to choose good or evil, life or death, and that the unrepentant bring condemnation and a second spiritual death upon themselves.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The Lord commands Samuel, through his angel, to prophesy and call the people to repent. The Lord’s judgments await the people because of their iniquities.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: God gives people knowledge and makes them free to choose good or evil, life or death.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, and the Creator of all things. His death brings the resurrection and redeems mankind from the first spiritual death.

l: an angel of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The angel commands Samuel to prophesy and tells him about the signs that will accompany the death of Jesus Christ, including darkness, thunderings and lightnings, tempests, and other upheavals.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The people become angry with Samuel because he is a Lamanite and speaks hard words against them, and they seek to destroy him and cast him out. They are told to hear his words, know God’s judgments, and learn the conditions of repentance.

l: believers in the Son of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Believers in the Son of God shall have everlasting life. Those who believe on his name may be saved.

l: the unrepentant, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The unrepentant are hewn down and cast into the fire. They suffer a second spiritual death and bring condemnation upon themselves.

l: earth, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The earth shall shake and tremble, its rocks shall be broken into seams, cracks, and fragments, and its mountains and valleys shall be changed. Highways shall be broken up and many cities shall become desolate.

l: the land, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The land shall have no light for three days when Jesus Christ suffers death. Signs and wonders shall come to pass across the land.

l: the presence of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The fall of Adam cuts all mankind off from the presence of the Lord, and the resurrection of Christ brings mankind back into that presence.

l: the sign of Christ’s coming, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The sign of Christ’s coming includes great lights in heaven, a darknessless night before he is born, a new star, and many signs and wonders in heaven.

l: the coming of Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The coming of Jesus Christ shall occur after five years, and signs will be given so people may know of it and believe on his name.

l: the birth of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The night before Jesus Christ is born shall not be dark, and it shall appear as if it were day. A new star shall arise as a sign of his birth.

l: the suffering and death of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: At the death of Jesus Christ, the sun, moon, and stars shall give no light for three days. Thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, tempests, broken rocks, changed landscapes, and opened graves shall accompany his death.

l: the resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The resurrection of Jesus Christ redeems all mankind and brings them back into the presence of the Lord. It also brings to pass the condition of repentance.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Repentance allows people to receive a remission of their sins through the merits of Jesus Christ. Those who repent are not hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: salvation, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Salvation comes through the death of Jesus Christ, and those who believe on the Son of God may be saved.

l: iniquity, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: People are called to repent of all their sins so they may receive a remission of them through the merits of Jesus Christ.

l: spiritual death, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The first spiritual death comes through the fall of Adam, which cuts mankind off from the presence of the Lord. A second spiritual death comes upon those who do not repent.

l: the fall of Adam, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The fall of Adam cuts all mankind off from the presence of the Lord, leaving them considered dead in temporal and spiritual things.

l: the darknessless night, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The night before Jesus Christ is born shall have no darkness and shall appear to people as if it were day.

l: the new star, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: A new star shall arise as a sign of the birth of Jesus Christ, unlike any star previously seen.

l: the darkening of the sun, moon, and stars, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: At the death of Jesus Christ, the sun shall be darkened and refuse to give its light, and the moon and stars shall also give no light for three days.

l: thunderings and lightnings, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Thunderings and lightnings shall continue for many hours when Jesus Christ yields up the ghost.

l: the earthquake, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The earth shall shake and tremble when Jesus Christ yields up the ghost.

l: the tempests, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Great tempests shall occur during the signs accompanying the death of Jesus Christ, while darkness covers the whole earth for three days.

l: good and evil, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: God gives people knowledge to distinguish good from evil. People may choose good and be restored to good, or choose evil and have evil restored to them.

l: free agency, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: People are free and permitted to act for themselves. They may choose life or death and bring upon themselves the consequences of their choices.

l: life or death, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: People are given the choice of life or death. They can choose good and be restored to good, or choose evil and have evil restored to them.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lord warns the people of Nephi that unless they repent, they will be utterly destroyed despite the signs and wonders and mighty works shown to them. The Lamanites receive salvation through the preaching of the Nephites, and many follow the path of duty, keep the commandments, and strive to bring others to knowledge of the truth. Those Lamanites who gain knowledge of the truth, believe the holy scriptures, and repent experience a change of heart, become firm and steadfast in faith, and bury their weapons of war. The Lord promises mercy and the restoration of the Lamanites to knowledge of the truth, while declaring that the people of Nephi will be destroyed if they remain in unbelief and do not repent.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lord chastens the people of Nephi because he loves them and prolongs the days of the Lamanites so they may receive salvation. He promises mercy to the Lamanites and declares that he will utterly destroy the people of Nephi if they do not repent and observe his will.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The people of Nephi are warned to repent after witnessing signs and wonders and mighty works. If they remain in unbelief and do not repent, the Lord will utterly destroy them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lamanites receive salvation through the preaching of the Nephites, and the more part of them walk circumspectly before God and keep his commandments. They are promised mercy and restoration to knowledge of the truth despite future afflictions, scattering, and being hunted.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Christ is the object of the faith of those Lamanites who would rather be trodden down and slain than lift their swords against their enemies.

l: signs and wonders, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Signs and wonders are shown to the people of Nephi, who are warned to repent when they see them.

l: mighty works, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Mighty works have been shown to the people of Nephi. The Lord says the Lamanites who dwindled in unbelief would not have done so again if those mighty works had been shown to them.

l: salvation, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Salvation comes to the Lamanites through the preaching of the Nephites.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The people of Nephi are repeatedly commanded to repent or face destruction. Among the Lamanites, faith and repentance bring a change of heart.

l: faith, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Faith in the Lord and the holy scriptures makes those Lamanites who gain knowledge of the truth firm and steadfast. Because of their faith in Christ, they fear to take up their buried weapons of war.

l: unbelief, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lamanites may dwindle in unbelief, but the Lord will prolong their days until the promised restoration. The people of Nephi face utter destruction because of their unbelief despite the mighty works done among them.

l: iniquity, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lord chastens the people of Nephi in the days of their iniquities because he loves them. The iniquity of the traditions of the fathers is identified as the reason for the Lamanites' evil deeds.

l: knowledge of the truth, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Lamanites who are brought to knowledge of the truth and learn of the wicked traditions of their fathers are led to believe the holy scriptures, have faith and repentance, and experience a change of heart. The Lamanites are promised restoration to knowledge of the truth.

l: traditions of their fathers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The traditions of the fathers are described as the cause of the Lamanites' iniquity and as a reason some dwindle in unbelief. Learning that these traditions are wicked helps bring the Lamanites to belief and repentance.

l: weapons of war, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Those Lamanites who become firm and steadfast in faith bury their weapons of war. They fear to take them up and will suffer themselves to be trodden down and slain rather than sin by fighting their enemies.

l: restoration of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The restoration of the Lamanites is prophesied as their return to knowledge of the truth and knowledge of their Redeemer and great and true shepherd. They will be numbered among his sheep.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Samuel, the Lamanite, preached from the walls, and those who believed his words sought Nephi, confessed their sins, and were baptized. Unbelievers attacked Samuel with stones and arrows, but the Spirit of the Lord protected him, and he fled to his own country. During the ninetieth year of the reign of the judges, signs, wonders, miracles, and angels appeared as the words of the prophets began to be fulfilled, but most of the people hardened their hearts. Satan spread rumors and contentions, and the people increasingly depended on their own strength and wisdom.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Nephi baptized, prophesied, preached repentance, showed signs and wonders, and worked miracles. Those who believed Samuel's words went to Nephi, confessed their sins, and sought baptism.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Lord was the one unto whom people desired to be baptized.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: God was the one before whom the lesser part of the people walked more circumspectly.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Christ was taught to be coming shortly, and the people argued that it was not reasonable that such a being as a Christ would come.

l: Satan, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Satan stirred the people to do iniquity continually, spread rumors and contentions across the land, and hardened their hearts against what was good and what should come.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Nephites were among the people who began to harden their hearts and depend on their own strength and wisdom.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Lamanites were among the people affected by hardening hearts and dependence on their own strength and wisdom.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The people of Nephi were governed under the reign of the judges, and most remained in pride and wickedness while a lesser part walked more circumspectly before God.

l: believers in Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Believers in Samuel's words sought Nephi, confessed their sins, and were baptized. Their number increased after people saw that Samuel could not be struck by stones or arrows.

l: unbelievers in Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Unbelievers in Samuel's words became angry, attacked Samuel with stones and arrows, and sought to bind him, saying that he had a devil.

l: the holy prophets, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The words of the prophets began to be fulfilled in the ninetieth year of the reign of the judges.

l: angels of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Angels appeared unto men, including wise men, and declared glad tidings of great joy.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Jerusalem was described as a land where Christ would show himself to people.

l: the land, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The people questioned why Christ would not show himself in this land as well as in the land of Jerusalem.

l: Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Samuel's words led believers to repentance and baptism, while unbelievers rejected them and attacked Samuel.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The word was taught by those whom the people depended upon, and some feared that this dependence would keep them in ignorance.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Spirit of the Lord was with Samuel and prevented stones and arrows from hitting him.

l: the evil one, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The unbelievers accused Samuel of having a devil, claiming that the devil's power prevented them from hitting him.

l: baptism, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Baptism was sought by those who believed Samuel's words and came repenting and confessing their sins.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Repentance was preached by Nephi, and believers in Samuel's words came repenting and confessing their sins.

l: preaching, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Samuel preached and prophesied among his own people, while Nephi preached repentance among the people.

l: prophecies, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Samuel and Nephi prophesied, and the words of the prophets began to be fulfilled.

l: signs and wonders, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Nephi showed signs and wonders so the people might know that Christ must shortly come.

l: miracles, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Nephi worked miracles among the people, and miracles were also wrought among the people of the Lord.

l: the coming of Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The coming of Christ was taught as something that must shortly come, but most of the people doubted that it would occur among them.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The people increasingly did what was contrary to the commandments of God in the eighty-ninth year of the reign of the judges.

l: pride, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Most of the people remained in pride at the end of the eighty-seventh year of the reign of the judges.

l: iniquity, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Most of the people remained in wickedness, and the people began to do more and more iniquity.

l: rumors and contentions, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Rumors and contentions were spread across the land by Satan to harden the hearts of the people.

l: tradition, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The people called the teaching about Christ a wicked tradition handed down by their fathers.

l: the reign of the judges, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The unit records events from the eighty-sixth through the ninetieth year of the reign of the judges and ends the book of Helaman.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Nephi (son of Helaman) departs from Zarahemla after entrusting the records to Nephi (son of Nephi), who keeps them. The prophecies of the prophets are fulfilled when the sign of the Lord's birth appears, including a night without darkness and a new star, and the people learn that the Lord will come into the world. Believers are preserved from a planned destruction, while many unbelievers are astonished, fear because of their iniquity and unbelief, and recognize that the Son of God must shortly appear. The people are baptized unto repentance and have peace, but the Gadianton robbers grow stronger as dissenters and some Lamanites join them.

l: Nephi (son of Helaman), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Nephi (son of Helaman) departs from the land of Zarahemla and gives charge of the plates of brass, the records, and the sacred things to his eldest son, Nephi (son of Nephi).

l: Nephi (son of Nephi), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Nephi (son of Nephi) keeps the records in place of Nephi (son of Helaman). When he sees the wickedness of the people and the threat against believers, he prays mightily to the Lord, receives the Lord's word, and later goes among the people baptizing unto repentance.

l: Samuel the Lamanite, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Samuel the Lamanite is identified as the prophet whose words about the sign were rejected by some people, although the sign is fulfilled.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The Lord answers Nephi (son of Nephi), tells him to be of good cheer, and says that the sign will be given that night. The Lord declares that he will come into the world, fulfill the words of the holy prophets, and do the will of the Father and of the Son.

l: the Son of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The people begin to know that the Son of God must shortly appear after the sign is given.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The people are divided between believers and unbelievers over the prophecies. After the sign appears, many are astonished and fall to the earth, and the people later experience conversion, baptism, remission of sins, and peace, though the Gadianton robbers continue to cause slaughter.

l: believers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Believers become very sorrowful when unbelievers say the time for the prophecies has passed, but they watch steadfastly for the promised sign. A day is set apart for believers to be put to death unless the sign comes, and they are preserved when the sign appears.

l: unbelievers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Unbelievers say that the time for Samuel the Lamanite's words has passed and make a great uproar. They set a day to put believers to death, but when the sign appears many fall to the earth, become as if dead, and fear because of their iniquity and unbelief.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Some Nephites dissent and flee to the Gadianton robbers, causing sorrow among the Nephites who remain in the land.

l: Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites suffer sorrow as some of their children grow strong, are led away by Zoramites' lies and flattering words, and join the Gadianton robbers. The Lamanites begin to decrease in faith and righteousness because of the wickedness of the rising generation.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The Gadianton robbers dwell in the mountains and infest the land. Their strongholds and secret places prevent the people from overpowering them, and they commit many murders and much slaughter; they increase as dissenters and some Lamanites join them.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The prophets have testified for many years of the coming events, and their words are fulfilled when the promised sign appears and the Lord's birth occurs.

l: the law of Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Some people preach that it is no longer expedient to observe the law of Moses, but they err. They are converted and learn that the law must be fulfilled in every whit, with not one jot or tittle passing away until all is fulfilled.

l: the prophecies of the prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The prophecies of the prophets begin to be fulfilled more fully in the ninety and second year. They are fulfilled in the sign, the night without darkness, the new star, and the birth of the Lord.

l: the sign of the Lord's birth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The sign of the Lord's birth is given as promised: there is no darkness at the going down of the sun, and a new star appears according to the word. The people recognize that the sign has come and that the Lord should be born.

l: the night without darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The night without darkness is as light as mid-day, and the sun rises the next morning according to its proper order. This fulfills the sign given by the prophets.

l: the birth of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: The birth of the Lord is recognized by the people because the night without darkness and the other promised signs occur. The Lord declares that he will come into the world to fulfill all that has been spoken by the holy prophets.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman / Chapter 1
s: Believers watch steadfastly so they will know that their faith has not been vain. After the sign appears, many people believe and are converted unto the Lord, while the Lamanites later decrease in faith and righteousness because of wickedness.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people increasingly forget the signs and wonders, harden their hearts, and fall into wickedness under Satan’s influence. The Nephites and converted Lamanites unite against the numerous Gadianton robbers, whose violence threatens the land with destruction. The converted Lamanites are numbered among the Nephites, their curse is taken from them, and they are called Nephites. The war continues through the fifteenth year, with the outcome worsened by the wickedness, contentions, and dissensions of the people of Nephi.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people begin to forget the signs and wonders they had heard, become less astonished by signs from heaven, harden their hearts, and become blind in their minds. They disbelieve what they had heard and seen, grow strong in wickedness and abominations, and remain in wickedness despite preaching and prophesying.

l: signs and wonders, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people begin to forget the signs and wonders they had heard and become less astonished at signs or wonders from heaven. They begin to disbelieve all that they had heard and seen.

l: Satan, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Satan gets possession of the hearts of the people again, blinds their eyes, and leads them to believe that the doctrine of Christ is foolish and vain. He goes about leading away the hearts of the people, tempting them, and causing them to do great wickedness.

l: the doctrine of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people are led to believe that the doctrine of Christ is a foolish and vain thing.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people begin to wax strong in wickedness and abominations. Their wickedness, contentions, and dissensions give the Gadianton robbers many advantages over them.

l: Nephi (father of Nephi), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Nephi, who was the father of Nephi and had charge of the records, does not return to the land of Zarahemla and cannot be found anywhere in the land.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people reckon their time from the coming of Christ, and nine years have passed since the sign was given that the prophets said would precede Christ’s coming into the world.

l: the coming of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites begin to reckon their time from the period of the sign given or from the coming of Christ. Nine years have passed from that time.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The Gadianton robbers become numerous, slay many people, lay waste to many cities, and spread death and carnage throughout the land. The Nephites and converted Lamanites take up arms against them; the robbers are driven into the mountains and secret places, but later gain many advantages because of the wickedness and divisions among the people of Nephi.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites take up arms against the Gadianton robbers and are joined by converted Lamanites. They gain some advantage in the fourteenth year but suffer many afflictions and face destruction in the fifteenth year because of their iniquity.

l: Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Lamanites who become converted unto the Lord unite with the Nephites and take up arms against the Gadianton robbers for the safety of their lives, women, and children and to maintain their rights, church privileges, worship, freedom, and liberty.

l: converted Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The converted Lamanites unite with the Nephites against the Gadianton robbers and are numbered among the Nephites. Their curse is taken from them, their skin becomes white like the Nephites, and their young men and daughters become exceedingly fair; they are called Nephites.

l: the war between the Gadianton robbers and the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The war begins to cause wars and contentions throughout the land and becomes exceedingly sore. The Nephites gain some advantage in the fourteenth year, but the Gadianton robbers gain many advantages in the fifteenth year because of the wickedness, contentions, and dissensions of the people of Nephi.

l: destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites are threatened with utter destruction because of the war before the thirteenth year ends. By the fifteenth year, the sword of destruction hangs over the people, who are about to be smitten down because of their iniquity.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Giddianhi, the governor of the secret society of Gadianton, sends Lachoneus a letter demanding that the Nephites surrender their lands, possessions, cities, and government or face destruction. Lachoneus rejects the threat, calls the people to repentance and prayer, and gathers them with their families, animals, and possessions into the land of Zarahemla. The Nephites build strong fortifications and prepare armies under Gidgiddoni, who advises them to wait for the robbers to attack rather than invade the robbers’ lands. The people repent, pray for deliverance, and make weapons and armor in preparation for battle.

l: Lachoneus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Lachoneus receives Giddianhi’s threatening letter but is not frightened by it. He calls the people to gather, repent, pray, and prepare for the coming attack.

l: Giddianhi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Giddianhi identifies himself as governor of the secret society of Gadianton and demands that Lachoneus surrender the Nephites’ lands and possessions. He threatens to destroy the people if they refuse.

l: Gidgiddoni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Gidgiddoni is appointed chief commander of the Nephite armies and is described as a great prophet and the chief judge. He counsels the people to prepare in the center of their lands and wait for the robbers to attack.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites gather with their families, animals, grain, and possessions in the appointed land. They repent, pray for deliverance, build defenses, and prepare weapons and armor.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The Gadianton robbers threaten to attack and destroy the Nephites unless they surrender and join the robbers. They are led by Giddianhi and prepare to come down against the Nephites.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The people are instructed to cry unto the Lord for strength and deliverance. Gidgiddoni teaches that the Lord will deliver the robbers into their hands if they wait for the attack.

l: land of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The land of the Nephites is threatened by the Gadianton robbers. The people gather in one place within it to defend themselves.

l: Zarahemla, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The land of Zarahemla is appointed as the gathering place for the Nephites and their possessions. The people assemble there to defend themselves against their enemies.

l: fortifications, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Fortifications are built around the gathered people, and their strength is made exceedingly great.

l: armies, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Armies of the Nephites and those counted among the Nephites are placed as guards around the people day and night. Gidgiddoni is appointed to command them, and they prepare for battle.

l: letter from Giddianhi to Lachoneus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The letter praises Lachoneus’s firmness while demanding that he surrender the Nephites’ cities, lands, possessions, and government. It promises safety if they join the robbers and threatens destruction if they refuse.

l: liberty, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Giddianhi claims that his people are recovering rights and government, while Lachoneus and his people are described as defending their liberty and property.

l: rights and government, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Giddianhi says the robbers seek to recover their rights and government from those who have dissented away from them. He threatens to avenge their alleged wrongs.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Lachoneus teaches that the people must repent of all their iniquities to be delivered from the Gadianton robbers. The people repent of their sins.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Lachoneus causes the people to cry unto the Lord for strength. After gathering, they put up their prayers to the Lord for deliverance from their enemies.

l: battle against the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites prepare for battle by gathering their armies, building fortifications, and making weapons, armor, shields, and bucklers. Gidgiddoni directs them to wait for the robbers to attack.

l: threatened invasion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Giddianhi threatens to send his armies against the Nephites on the morrow month if they do not surrender. Lachoneus organizes the people and defenses in response to this threat.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The robbers, led first by Giddianhi and later by Zemnarihah, sought to take the deserted Nephite lands and force the Nephites to yield. Giddianhi’s armies attacked in the nineteenth year but were defeated and pursued by the Nephites, and Giddianhi was slain. In the twenty and first year, Zemnarihah led a siege, but the Nephites cut off the robbers’ retreat, captured many, and slew the remainder. The Nephites rejoiced and credited their deliverance to the Lord God, repentance, and humility.

l: Giddianhi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Giddianhi led the robbers and commanded them to battle against the Nephites because they could not otherwise subsist. His armies were defeated, and he was pursued, overtaken, and slain after much fighting.

l: Gidgiddoni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Gidgiddoni commanded the Nephite armies to pursue Giddianhi’s forces and slay those who fell into their hands. He later learned of the robbers’ retreat, placed armies in their path, and caused their forces to be cut off.

l: Zemnarihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Zemnarihah became the robbers’ leader and caused a siege to be laid around the Nephites. He commanded the robbers to withdraw, but he was captured and hanged upon a tree until he was dead.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites gathered into one body, stored provisions for seven years, and defended themselves against the robbers. They defeated Giddianhi’s armies, resisted Zemnarihah’s siege, captured many robbers, and rejoiced in their deliverance.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The robbers occupied deserted Nephite lands but lacked food and could not subsist except by plundering, robbing, and murdering. Their armies were defeated, suffered heavy losses and hunger, and many were captured while the remainder were slain.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The armies of the Nephites prayed for protection when they saw Giddianhi’s forces, then met them in the strength of the Lord. They pursued the robbers, blocked their retreat, and defeated them.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Lord God was supplicated by the Nephites for protection and deliverance from their enemies. The Nephites praised and thanked him for preserving them from destruction.

l: wilderness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The wilderness was the only place where the robbers could obtain food, but wild game there became scarce. The robbers were consequently about to perish with hunger.

l: battle against the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The battle against the Nephites began in the sixth month of the nineteenth year and was great and terrible, with unprecedented slaughter among the people of Lehi. The Nephites defeated Giddianhi’s armies and pursued them to the borders of the wilderness.

l: siege of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The robbers laid siege around the Nephites in the twenty and first year, intending to cut them off from their lands and outward privileges. The siege failed because the Nephites had abundant provisions and continually attacked the robbers.

l: slaughter, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The battle and subsequent pursuit produced great and terrible slaughter. The Nephites also caused great destruction among the robbers by attacking them by night and by day.

l: hanging of Zemnarihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Zemnarihah was captured and hanged upon a tree until he was dead. The tree was then felled, and the Nephites cried that those who sought to slay them through power and secret combinations should likewise be felled.

l: deliverance of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites were delivered from the hands of their enemies after defeating Giddianhi’s armies and ending Zemnarihah’s siege. They rejoiced, sang, praised God, and attributed their deliverance to repentance and humility.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Secret combinations were identified as a reason that enemies sought to slay the Nephites. The Nephites cried that those who sought to slay them because of power and secret combinations should be felled to the earth.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites knew that their repentance was a reason they had been delivered from everlasting destruction.

l: humility, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites knew that their humility was a reason they had been delivered from everlasting destruction.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites come to believe the prophets, recognize that Christ had come, forsake their sins, and serve God. They capture the robbers, preach the word of God to them, free those who repent and covenant not to murder, and punish those who refuse. Mormon explains that he is making a true record from earlier accounts and from what he has seen, and he testifies of Jesus Christ and the promises concerning the house of Jacob. The text teaches that the seed of Joseph and the seed of Jacob will be gathered from the earth and restored to knowledge of their covenant in the Lord’s due time.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites know that the words of the holy prophets must be fulfilled, that Christ had come, and that all things would come to pass as spoken. They forsake their sins and serve God with diligence.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Son of God and as the Redeemer. Mormon says he has been called by Jesus Christ to declare his word, and that the house of Jacob will know him.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The people serve God with diligence after forsaking their sins. Mormon blesses God and says that God brought their fathers from Jerusalem and gave him and his people knowledge unto salvation.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The robbers are taken prisoner, except those who are slain. Their prisoners are taught the word of God; those who repent and covenant not to murder are freed, while others are condemned and punished.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The wicked, secret, and abominable combinations are brought to an end, after the murders and wickedness associated with them.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi gave a shorter but true account of the proceedings of the people. Mormon makes his record according to Nephi’s record, which was engraved on the plates of Nephi.

l: Mormon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Mormon makes a record on plates with his own hands. He identifies himself as a disciple of Jesus Christ, a pure descendant of Lehi, and the recorder of events from earlier accounts and from what he has personally seen.

l: Lehi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Lehi left Jerusalem, and his descendants are called the children of Lehi. Mormon identifies himself as a pure descendant of Lehi.

l: Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Jerusalem is the land from which Lehi and those with him were brought out, though no one knew it except God and those whom he brought out.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The plates of Nephi are the plates on which Nephi’s record was engraved. Mormon makes his record according to that record.

l: record, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Mormon’s record is a small account covering events from the time Lehi left Jerusalem until Mormon’s present time. He says it is just and true, though many things cannot be written according to their language.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Lord has covenanted with the house of Jacob and will fulfill that covenant in his own due time. The house of Jacob will be restored to knowledge of the covenant and will know its Redeemer.

l: the remnant of the seed of Joseph, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Lord will again bring a remnant of the seed of Joseph to knowledge of the Lord their God.

l: seed of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The seed of Jacob is scattered across the earth, and the Lord will gather its remnant from the four quarters of the earth.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Those among the robbers who repent enter into a covenant that they will murder no more and are set at liberty. The covenant made with the house of Jacob will be fulfilled in the Lord’s due time.

l: the coming of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The people know that Christ had come because of the many signs given according to the prophets and because events had already occurred as spoken.

l: capture of the robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The robbers are captured, with none escaping except those who are slain. The prisoners are placed in prison and taught the word of God.

l: gathering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Lord will gather the remnant of the seed of Jacob from the four quarters of the earth and bring them to their own lands.

l: restoration of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The house of Jacob will be restored to knowledge of the covenant made with it. Its people will know Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and be gathered to their own lands.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Nephites returned to their lands with their families, possessions, provisions, and precious things, while lands were granted to repentant robbers who remained Lamanites, establishing peace and prosperity. Gidgiddoni, judge Lachoneus, and other leaders oversaw the peace, construction, roads, and laws, but pride, riches, learning differences, and persecution later caused inequality and the church to break up. Satan led the people into iniquity, and men sent from heaven preached about the sins of the people, the redemption the Lord would make, the resurrection of Christ, and Christ’s death and sufferings. Lawyers, judges, and high priests opposed these witnesses, secretly killed some prophets, and formed a covenant to defeat justice, destroy the governor, and establish a king.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Nephites returned to their own lands with their families, flocks, herds, horses, cattle, provisions, grain, gold, silver, and other precious things. They prospered, built and repaired cities, and later became involved in disputings, pride, persecutions, and iniquity.

l: Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Some robbers who entered into a covenant to keep the peace remained Lamanites and received lands according to their numbers. A few Lamanites were converted to the true faith and remained firm, steadfast, and immovable.

l: Gidgiddoni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Gidgiddoni, judge Lachoneus, and other appointed leaders established great peace in the land.

l: Lachoneus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Lachoneus, together with Gidgiddoni and other appointed leaders, established great peace in the land.

l: Lachoneus the younger, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Lachoneus the younger filled the seat of his father and governed the people in the thirtieth year.

l: Satan, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Satan had great power to stir up the people to iniquity and puff them up with pride, tempting them to seek power, authority, riches, and the vain things of the world. He led the people away from God and carried them about by his temptations.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Men sent from heaven testified of Jesus Christ’s death and sufferings and of the resurrection of Christ.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The people knew the will of God because it had been taught to them, yet they wilfully rebelled against God. Some who suffered persecution were humble and penitent before God.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The prophets of the Lord were condemned to death by judges acting contrary to the law. The Lord’s people were targeted by a covenant formed to destroy them.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The people returned to their lands, prospered, established order, and lived in peace before becoming divided by riches, learning, pride, and poverty. They later reached a state of awful wickedness and some opposed those who testified of Christ.

l: church, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The church began to be broken up because of great inequality and, in the thirtieth year, was broken up throughout the land except among a few converted Lamanites.

l: lawyers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: There were many lawyers in the land, and they were among those angered by testimony concerning Christ. Almost all the lawyers joined with the kindreds and friends of judges accused of unlawfully killing prophets.

l: judges, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Some judges secretly put witnesses of Christ to death without the governor’s authorization. The accused judges had many friends and kindreds, and they joined a covenant to defeat justice, destroy the governor, and establish a king.

l: high priests, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Some high priests were among those angered by testimony concerning Christ. Almost all the high priests joined with the kindreds of the judges who were to be tried.

l: prophets of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Prophets who testified of things pertaining to Christ were secretly taken and put to death by judges. A complaint was brought against the judges for condemning them contrary to the law.

l: country, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The land experienced peace, prosperity, repaired and newly built cities, highways, and roads. Later, inequality and wickedness spread throughout the land, and conspirators sought to make it subject to a king.

l: riches, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Great riches caused some people to become proud and boastful and contributed to distinctions by rank. Riches also gave some people access to great learning, while poverty left others ignorant.

l: laws, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The people formed laws according to equity and justice. The law prohibited anyone from being put to death without power from the governor, but judges violated this law.

l: peace, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Peace was established throughout the land and continued for several years. It ended as disputings, pride, persecution, and iniquity increased.

l: pride, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Pride arose among people because of their exceedingly great riches and contributed to boastings, persecutions, inequality, and the breaking up of the church.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The people’s iniquity was caused by Satan’s influence and included seeking power, authority, riches, and worldly things. The people knowingly and wilfully rebelled against God.

l: redemption, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Men sent from heaven testified concerning the redemption which the Lord would make for his people.

l: resurrection of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Men inspired from heaven testified boldly concerning the resurrection of Christ.

l: covenant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Some robbers entered into a covenant to keep the peace and were granted lands. Later, lawyers, judges, high priests, and kindreds entered into a covenant administered by the devil to oppose righteousness, free murderers from justice, destroy the governor, and establish a king.

l: justice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The judges’ unlawful killings led to a complaint and a trial intended to administer justice according to the law. The conspirators united to deliver the guilty from justice.

l: king, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The conspirators covenanted to destroy the governor and establish a king so that the land would no longer be at liberty but would be subject to kings.
